title: Finite integer-valued unit map for an integral scheme over an algebraically closed field
statement: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $T$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] locally of finite type over $K$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Write $B=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ and $B^\times$ for the multiplicative group of invertible elements of $B$. There exist a finite set $J$ and a map $v:B^\times\to\mathbf Z^J$, where $\mathbf Z^J$ is the additive group of functions $J\to\mathbf Z$, such that $v(ab)=v(a)+v(b)$ for all $a,b\in B^\times$ and $\ker(v)=K^\times$. Here $K^\times\subset B^\times$ is the subgroup of nonzero constant functions, and $\ker(v)$ consists of the units sent to the zero function. No separatedness or quasi-compactness assumption on $T$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 04L5 (lemma-units-integral-finite-type-algebraically-closed), proof by restriction to an affine open and normalization of a projective closure; Tag 04L4 (lemma-open-in-normal-proper), proof, displayed finite valuation map and its kernel. The map on T is the composite of restriction, pullback to the normal open, and that displayed map.

proof.text: Choose a nonempty affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ from a finite-type affine chart of $T\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. Thus $A$ is a finitely generated $K$-algebra and a domain. Put $F=\mathcal O_{T,\eta}$ at the generic point. For every nonempty affine open $W\subset T$, its section ring injects into $F$ by the affine-fraction-field lemma. Consequently $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)\to F$ is injective: a section with zero generic germ restricts to zero on each such $W$, hence is zero by the sheaf axiom. In particular restriction to $U$ is injective, and $F=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ with its specified $K$-algebra structure. This argument uses no quasi-compactness or separatedness of $T$.

source.place: Tag 04L5 (lemma-units-integral-finite-type-algebraically-closed), first paragraph; Tag 01RV for generic germs

proof.text: An affine scheme is quasi-affine (use the identity open immersion). Apply the affine-space immersion existence lemma to $U/K$, then the affine projective-closure lemma over the Noetherian scheme $\operatorname{Spec}K$. It supplies a projective, hence proper, scheme $C$ containing $U$ as a dense open, with $C$ the scheme-theoretic image of $U\to\mathbf P^n_K$. The reduced-image lemma says that $C$ is reduced because $U$ is reduced. Its underlying space is the closure of the irreducible nonempty space $U$, hence is irreducible and nonempty. Thus $C$ is integral, and its generic stalk is the same $F$, since the open immersion is an isomorphism on neighbourhoods of the common generic point.

source.place: Tag 04L5, first paragraph: affine embedding and projective closure; Tag 056B (morphisms.tex, lemma-scheme-theoretic-image-reduced)

proof.text:
Take the normalization $
u:N	o C$ in $F$, applying finite-normalization functoriality with the degree-one extension $M=H=F$. It says that $N$ is normal integral and Noetherian, $
u$ is finite surjective, and $k(N)$ is canonically $F$. The properness clause of normalization-exists makes $N$ proper because $C$ is proper. Let $V=
u^{-1}(U)$; it is a nonempty open by surjectivity. The maps on generic stalks are the specified identification with $F$, so restriction to $U$ followed by pullback to $V$ sends every $a\in B^	imes$ to the rational function $ho(a)\in F^	imes$ given by its generic germ in step 1. This function and its inverse are regular on $V$. The map $ho$ is injective and respects the $K$-algebra structure.

Since $C$ is proper it is quasi-compact. Choose a finite cover by nonempty affine opens $C_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$; discard any empty chart. Finiteness of $\nu$ makes $W_i=\nu^{-1}(C_i)$ affine, and these form a finite cover of $N$. The affine normalization formula, specialized to the integral scheme $C$ (whose unique minimal prime on each chart is $(0)$), identifies $W_i=\operatorname{Spec}D_i$, where $D_i$ is the integral closure of $R_i$ in $F$. That formula says the affine section rings of $N$ are Noetherian. The integral-closure normality lemma with $L=F$ shows that each $D_i$ is a normal domain with fraction field $F$. Thus all the hypotheses of the affine principal-divisor kernel theorem hold for each $D_i$.

source.place: Tag 04L4 (lemma-open-in-normal-proper), affine chart paragraph; morphisms.tex Tags 0C3B/0CDV; algebra.tex Tag 034L

proof.text: Let $E=N\setminus V$, a closed subset of the Noetherian scheme $N$. Its irreducible components are finite in number, and each has a generic point by scheme sobriety. Let $J_i$ be the height-one primes of $D_i$ whose points lie in $E$. For $\mathfrak q\in J_i$, let $Z$ be a component of $E$ containing its point $x$, and let $\zeta$ be the generic point of $Z$. Since $x\in W_i$ and $W_i$ is open, also $\zeta\in W_i$. In $\operatorname{Spec}D_i$, the prime $\mathfrak p$ of $\zeta$ satisfies $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q$. It is nonzero: $(0)$ is the generic point of the integral $N$, which belongs to the nonempty open $V$ and cannot lie in $E$. Height one now forces $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q$, so $x=\zeta$. Thus $J_i$ is contained in the finite set of generic points of the components of $E$. Put $J=\coprod_iJ_i$; the chart index set is finite, so $J$ is finite. This also handles $E=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 04L4, finite generic boundary points and codimension-one paragraph; properties.tex Tag 0BA8 (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components)

proof.text: For every height-one prime $\mathfrak q$ of $D_i$, the principal-divisor kernel theorem supplies the normalized additive valuation $v_{i,\mathfrak q}:F^\times\to\mathbf Z$ of $(D_i)_{\mathfrak q}$, its additivity, and the criterion $v_{i,\mathfrak q}(f)=0\iff f\in(D_i)_{\mathfrak q}^\times$. Define $v(a)(i,\mathfrak q)=v_{i,\mathfrak q}(\rho(a))$ for $(i,\mathfrak q)\in J$. Since generic germs respect multiplication and each valuation is additive, coordinatewise $v(ab)=v(a)+v(b)$. Repeated occurrences of a boundary point in different affine charts are allowed: $J$ indexes chart-prime pairs, and no independence of the coordinates is required.

source.place: Tags 00PD/031T and divisors.tex Tag 02RP (lemma-div-additive); varieties.tex Tag 04L4, displayed finite valuation map

proof.text: Suppose $v(a)=0$ and set $f=\rho(a)$. Fix $i$ and any height-one prime $\mathfrak q$ of $D_i$. If its point is outside $V$, it belongs to $J_i$, so $v_{i,\mathfrak q}(f)=0$ by assumption. If its point is in $V$, both $f$ and $f^{-1}$ are regular there by step 3. The affine stalk-localization theorem identifies their stalk with $(D_i)_{\mathfrak q}$; their germs multiply to $1$ there, so the valuation's unit criterion again gives $v_{i,\mathfrak q}(f)=0$. Thus the entire affine principal divisor of $f$ on $\operatorname{Spec}D_i$ is zero. The kernel clause of that theorem gives $f\in D_i^\times$. In particular $f$ and $f^{-1}$ define sections on every $W_i$.

source.place: Tag 04L4, kernel calculation using height-one affine localizations; algebra.tex Tag 031T

proof.text: The sections just obtained agree on overlaps: on every nonempty affine open contained in an overlap, their generic germs are the same element $f\in F$, and the affine-fraction-field lemma makes the germ map injective. The sheaf axiom glues them to $s\in\Gamma(N,\mathcal O_N)$; the sections representing $f^{-1}$ glue in the same way, and their products are $1$ on the cover, so $s$ is a unit. Since $N$ is integral, it is reduced, nonempty and irreducible, hence connected (a separation into two nonempty opens contradicts irreducibility). Apply the proper-reduced global-sections theorem over the algebraically closed field $K$: its component-indexed constant map is an isomorphism. Here the component set has one element, so its assertion is exactly that $K\to\Gamma(N,\mathcal O_N)$ is an isomorphism of $K$-algebras. Therefore $s=c$ for some $c\in K^\times$.

source.place: Tag 04L4, extension to the proper variety and constant functions; Tag 0BUG (lemma-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections), reduced algebraically closed specialization

proof.text: Taking the generic germ of $s=c$ gives $\rho(a)=c$ in the specified $K$-field $F$. The injectivity in step 1 yields $a=c$ in $B$, so $\ker(v)\subseteq K^\times$. Conversely any $c\in K^\times$ and its inverse are regular on all of $N$. They are units in every $(D_i)_{\mathfrak q}$; the same unit criterion gives every coordinate $v(c)(i,\mathfrak q)=0$. Thus $K^\times\subseteq\ker(v)$. The finite $J$ and the map constructed in step 6 satisfy all the required clauses, including when $J$ is empty.
